canonical_title: White House finalizes voluntary cybersecurity testing framework for frontier AI models
aliases: White House voluntary AI cyber tests
Trump administration AI model cyber tests
government pre-release frontier model cyber testing
organizations: Office of the National Cyber Director
treatment: Treat as a U.S. government frontier-model cyber evaluation framework topic. The June executive-order mandate, August 3 framework finalization, and August 4 industry-meeting decision to exclude open-weight models from voluntary testing are covered. Reinclude only for published test metrics, threshold definitions, reporting rules, participating-model results, formal developer commitments, mandatory requirements, changes to the open-weight exemption, or other material implementation changes.
known_facts: A June 2026 executive order directed U.S. agencies to develop a classified benchmarking process for advanced cyber capabilities and a voluntary framework allowing developers to provide covered frontier models to the Federal Government for up to 30 days before wider trusted-partner release.
Reuters reported on 2026-08-03 that the White House had finalized details of voluntary cybersecurity tests intended to measure the hacking capabilities of the most advanced U.S. AI models.
Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Nvidia discussed the unpublished framework with White House officials on 2026-08-04.
Reuters reported after the meeting that the administration told developers it would not put open-weight models such as Meta Llama and Nvidia Nemotron through the voluntary safety tests.
The White House had not publicly disclosed the specific test metrics, result-reporting method, or full framework text as of the August 4 meeting.
Five Democratic senators called for legislation making testing permanent for the most advanced American-made frontier models.
The framework remains voluntary and does not itself establish a mandatory licensing, preclearance, or permitting requirement for model release.
reinclude_only_if: The White House, ONCD, Commerce, NIST, NSA, or CISA publishes the test suite, covered-frontier-model threshold, metrics, reporting rules, or implementation guidance.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, or another frontier lab formally joins, declines, or materially conditions participation.
The government publishes results from testing a specific model or changes a model release based on the framework.
Congress or the administration converts the voluntary framework into a binding reporting, licensing, pre-release access, or enforcement requirement.
The administration changes or removes the open-weight model exemption.
A material security incident causes the framework to be revised or expanded.
notes: Adopted as the 2026-08-04 Midday delta. Updated 2026-08-05 Midday with the post-meeting exclusion of open-weight models from voluntary testing. Distinct from incident-specific OpenAI/Anthropic regulatory follow-ups because this is a cross-industry federal testing framework.
